title: Fanout resilience mosaic and circuit-breaker replay for token-level SLI instrumentation
creator: Priya Sharma
description: Background: We need richer instrumentation that ties token-level latency SLIs to the live fanout topology and the state transitions of regional circuit breakers. Current dashboards surface p99 per-route and coarse region failovers, but engineers cannot answer: (1) which upstream shard/fanout path amplified tail latency for a given key, (2) whether a circuit-breaker transition preceded or followed token-level p99 spikes, or (3) how a replay of failing requests would flow through fallback paths. This ticket implements an instrumentation + dashboard pattern (the 'mosaic') that stitches together token traces, fanout maps, and circuit state timelines, plus a reproducible replay harness for deterministically exercising failover logic.
goals: 1) Emit enriched telemetry linking token-id -> fanout path -> serving-shard -> circuit-state at time-of-admit. 2) New dashboard panels to visualize mosaic views (topology heatmap, token waterfall annotated with circuit transitions, and aggregated fanout failure rates). 3) A replay controller that can re-run a sample of historical requests against current routing logic to validate rollback/fallback behavior. 4) Instrumentation must be sample-safe (bounded cardinality) and compatible with existing token-SLI pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: - Telemetry: for 95% of sampled tokens, p95/p99 rows show attached fields: fanout_path (list of ephemeral ids), shard_id, circuit_state_before, circuit_state_after, admit_latency_ms, kv_cache_hit. - Dashboard: Mosaic view with 3 linked panels (topology heatmap, annotated token waterfall, circuit timeline) deployed to Grafana folder 'SLO/Mosaic'. - Alerts: New alert 'Mosaic-Token-P99-Surge' triggers on sustained p99 > 500ms for 5m with customer_impact >= medium. - Replay harness: can replay a saved 30-minute sample against staging routing and produce a comparison report (baseline vs replay) with diffs in fallback counts and avg token latency. - No increase in production telemetry cost beyond 12% budget projection (doc attached).

design_notes: - Use hashed token_id (prefix only) to prevent PII leakage; attach sample_id not raw token. - fanout_path format: comma-separated short ids (region:shard:route) with max depth 6. - circuit_state should be {OPEN|CLOSED|HALF_OPEN} encoded as enum string. - Emit a light-weight delta event when circuit transitions to avoid scanning full timelines. - Sampling: combine deterministic reservoir sampling per-customer for reproducible replays plus low-rate random samples for system coverage. - Storage: sampled traces go to a short-term TTL store (14 days) and to the replay index. - Cost guardrails: cap enriched telemetry to 0.5% of total requests by default; opt-in per-project via label.
dashboard_queries: Topology heatmap: count(errors) by fanout_path_prefix and region over 5m; query uses aggregated tag fanout_path_prefix (first two hops)
Token waterfall: raw admits for sampled token_ids with per-token per-step latency metrics and an overlay of circuit_state timestamps; join admit_logs and circuit_events by sample_id and time_window
Circuit timeline: timeseries of circuit_state transitions by shard_id with annotations for admit spikes and failovers
Replay diff: table view comparing baseline vs replay counts for fallback invocations by route and avg token latency delta
notes_and_tradeoffs: - Tradeoff: attaching fanout_path increases tag cardinality; mitigated via prefixing and fixed-depth truncation. - Tradeoff: richer circuit snapshots could add latency to admit; therefore we emit a light delta on transition and store full snapshots only for sampled requests. - We considered streaming full traces to Jaeger but decided on compact JSON lines to reduce ingestion cost. - Replay harness will require test-only shims for authentication; ensure replay runs in a sandboxed routing mode.

Rollout: dark launch -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with cost telemetry gating (7d)
